name: Complement cascade
summary: Three ways in, one way out. Classical (C1 on IgG/IgM–antigen complexes) and lectin (MBL on microbial mannose) cut C4 and C2 into C4b2a; the alternative pathway (spontaneous C3 on microbial surfaces, factor B, factor D) makes C3bBb. Both C3 convertases cut C3: C3b opsonizes and joins them to make C5 convertases; C3a and C5a are anaphylatoxins (C5a also draws neutrophils). C5b with C6–C9 forms the membrane attack complex, which lyses Neisseria. Regulators: C1 inhibitor (HAE), DAF/CD55 and CD59 (PNH), factor H.
tissue: blood plasma and tissue fluid (made mostly in the liver)

c42.name: C4 + C2
c42.notes: Cleaved into C4b and C2a, which join on the microbe’s surface. C2 or C4 deficiency raises the risk of SLE.

c3b_fb.name: C3(H₂O) + factor B
c3b_fb.notes: C3 hydrolyzes on its own all the time (tickover); on a microbe’s surface, with no host regulators to stop it, the product binds factor B.

c4b2a.name: C4b2a
c4b2a.notes: The C3 convertase of the classical and lectin pathways (newer naming: C4b2b). Decay-accelerating factor (DAF, CD55) takes it apart on host cells.

c3bbb.name: C3bBb
c3bbb.notes: The C3 convertase of the alternative pathway; properdin stabilizes it, factor H and DAF take it apart. Every C3b it makes can make another: an amplification loop.

c3.name: C3
c3.notes: The hub of all three pathways. C3 deficiency: severe, recurrent pyogenic infections (sinus, respiratory) and immune complex disease.

c3b.name: C3b
c3b.notes: The main opsonin (with IgG): coats microbes for phagocytosis. Also joins the C3 convertases to make the C5 convertases, and clears immune complexes.

c4b2a3b.name: C4b2a3b
c4b2a3b.notes: The C5 convertase of the classical and lectin pathways.

c3bbb3b.name: C3bBb3b
c3bbb3b.notes: The C5 convertase of the alternative pathway.

c5.name: C5
c5.notes: Eculizumab binds C5 and blocks its cleavage (PNH, atypical HUS); it raises the risk of Neisseria infection, so patients are vaccinated.

mac.name: Membrane attack complex (C5b–9)
mac.notes: A pore that lyses cells, most importantly Neisseria. Deficiency of C5–C9: recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal, gonococcal) infection. CD59 (protectin) keeps it off host cells; without CD59 and DAF (PNH), red cells lyse.

c1.name: C1 (C1q, C1r, C1s)
c1.notes: Classical pathway: C1q binds antibody on an antigen (IgM best, or two IgG; GM makes classic: IgG and IgM). C1 esterase inhibitor keeps it in check; its deficiency causes hereditary angioedema (with high bradykinin; avoid ACE inhibitors).

masp.name: MBL–MASP
masp.notes: Lectin pathway: mannose-binding lectin binds mannose on microbe surfaces, and its MASP proteases cleave C4 and C2 like C1s.

fd.name: Factor D
fd.notes: Cuts factor B (to Bb) once it has bound C3b.

addc3b_cl.name: C3b joins C4b2a
addc3b_cl.notes: A C3b sitting next to the C3 convertase turns it into a C5 convertase.

mac_asm.name: MAC assembly (C6–C9)
mac_asm.notes: C5b gathers C6, C7, C8 and then many C9s into a pore.

groups.name: Classical and lectin pathways
groups.notes: Classical: C1 bound to IgG or IgM on antigen (“GM makes classic cars”). Lectin: mannose-binding lectin on microbial sugars. Both cleave C4 and C2.

groups.name: Alternative pathway
groups.notes: Spontaneous C3 hydrolysis on microbial surfaces; factor B and factor D; properdin stabilizes C3bBb.

groups.name: Terminal pathway
groups.notes: C5b joins C6–C9 to form the membrane attack complex. C5–C9 deficiency: recurrent Neisseria infections. Eculizumab blocks C5.
